Pinned certificate (SHA-256): `{fingerprint}`

Whenever Comexio serves HTTPS, the integration connects encrypted and pins the certificate automatically. HTTP means Comexio serves no HTTPS: the connection is not encrypted.

reconfigure_http.title: Switch to unencrypted HTTP?

**{host}** answered no HTTPS. The pinned certificate:
`{pinned}`

If you continue, Home Assistant connects over plain HTTP — unencrypted, including the admin login — and drops the pinned certificate. The next start pins whatever certificate Comexio then presents.

If Comexio should serve HTTPS (or is just not reachable right now), close this dialog and nothing changes.

reconfigure_certificate.title: Trust another certificate?

`{pinned}`

Presented (SHA-256):
`{actual}`

Compare the presented value with the SHA-256 Comexio’s admin page lists under its certificate hashes. Continue only if they match — then the new certificate is pinned. Otherwise close this dialog and nothing changes.

data_description.logikplan_plan_prefix: Prefix for auto-created cluster plans. Plans are named like: HA - Marker [1-100].
data_description.logikplan_max_pairs_per_plan: How many Web-IO + marker pairs fit into one managed plan before a new cluster plan is created. For IO and Quickbus cluster plans this maps to 1 (50), 2 (100) or 3 (150) columns per plan: one extension per column, while Quickbus devices stack in a column as long as they fit. KNX cluster plans ignore this setting and always use a fixed size of 50.
data_description.logikplan_io_extensions: Each selected extension gets its IOs wired into a managed IO cluster plan (e.g. HA - IO [Ext]), one column per extension. Start with a single extension to test, then add the others.
data_description.logikplan_quickbus_devices: Each selected Quickbus device gets its IOs wired into a managed QB cluster plan (e.g. HA - QB [1,3], named by device id), stacked in the plan's columns, so Comexio pushes their values to Home Assistant. Read-only: Comexio offers no way to write a Quickbus IO. All devices are selected until you change it; only selected devices get Web-IO commands.
data_description.ignored_markers: Comma-, semicolon-, space- or dot-separated marker IDs and ranges, with or without 'M' prefix (e.g. '123, 456; 789' or 'M123, M456' or '8-12'). Only markers with a description can be ignored. A single ID that no longer exists is removed automatically; a range stays as written and also covers IDs created later.
data_description.ignored_knx: Comma-, semicolon-, space- or dot-separated KNX object IDs and ranges, with or without 'K' prefix (e.g. '123, 456; 789' or 'K123, K456' or '8-12'). Only KNX objects with a description can be ignored. A single ID that no longer exists is removed automatically; a range stays as written and also covers IDs created later.
data_description.function_plan_backup_retention_months: Once the newest backup of a plan that was deleted directly in Comexio is older than this, a repair asks whether to delete or keep that plan's backups — nothing is deleted without your confirmation. A live plan's backups are never affected. The 'Function Plan Purge Orphaned Backups' action deletes all expired ones at once.
data_description.bus_watchdog_enabled: On a sustained bus-load rise, automatically restart the HA-managed cluster function plans (back to front) to try to relieve it. Non-destructive to the Comexio system itself.
data_description.bus_watchdog_auto_reboot: If the bus load averages above 90% for 5 minutes, trigger an IMMEDIATE, unconfirmed full Comexio system reboot. Off by default — enable only once you trust the watchdog.
data_description.function_plan_watchdog_notify: Notify services (e.g. notify.mobile_app_your_phone) that get a push when a watched function plan stops (HA-managed, or a user plan picked below). The push has a 'Start plan' button, and is removed again once the plan runs. A watched user plan deleted in Comexio gets a push too, with 'Restore' (its newest backup, as a new plan) and 'Stop watching' buttons; if its ID now holds another plan (renamed, or the ID reused), only 'Stop watching' — restore it or take the rename over in its repair. They also get an urgent push when Comexio presents another TLS certificate than the pinned one. Leave empty for no push; the repair is raised either way.
data_description.function_plan_watchdog_user_plans: User plans (not managed by Home Assistant) that should always run. The watchdog treats them like the HA plans: repair, problem sensor and push when one stops. The Plan Auto-Start (user plans) switch starts them again on its own. A picked plan deleted in Comexio is not started: its repair and push offer to restore it from its newest backup or to stop watching it. A plan renamed in Comexio with its content unchanged is followed on its own (its pick and backups take the new name). If its ID now holds another plan (renamed, or the ID reused), the repair also offers to watch that plan instead or, its content matching the last backup, to take it over as the plan renamed (its backups move along). Leave plans you stop on purpose (tests) out.
data_description.webhook_address_mode: Where Comexio sends live values. Automatic: HA's local address. External HA URL: host and port of the external URL from HA's network settings (https without a port means 443). Custom address: a URL you enter in the next step. With an external or custom address, the push leaves your network and goes over the internet. Run a Web-IO sync afterwards.

data_description.webhook_url: Base URL of Home Assistant as Comexio should reach it, e.g. {example_url} — no path. The push then goes over the internet if this address is public.

uninstall_cleanup.title: Uninstall Cleanup
uninstall_cleanup.description:
Choose what to remove from Comexio. In total, the integration created {plan_count} Function Plan(s), {device_count} Web-IO device(s), and {class_count} Web-IO class(es).

* **Everything** removes all of it.
* **Markers only / IOs only / KNX only / Quickbus only** remove just that part's Function Plans, Web-IO device and class. The shared trigger plan is only removed as a whole if it holds no trigger pairs of the other category — otherwise Markers/KNX remove just their own pairs from it.
* **KNX only** and **Everything** also clear the titles of unused KNX bridge markers, so they become free markers again. A bridge marker you use in an own Function Plan only loses its [K…], [RO] and [TRIG] suffixes and stays a plain marker with its start value. The markers themselves are not deleted.

This cannot be undone. Deleted Function Plans lose their wiring permanently.

uninstall_cleanup.description:
This installation still contains KNX Function Plans or Web-IO devices from a KNX pre-release (v0.10.0-rc1 to rc3). Their layout no longer matches this version.

**KNX only** (preselected) removes the KNX Function Plans, the KNX Web-IO device and class and the KNX loopback Web-IO, and clears the titles of unused KNX bridge markers so they can be reused (one used in an own Function Plan only loses its suffixes). The next sync then rebuilds everything cleanly. Marker and IO plans are not touched; from the shared trigger plan only the KNX trigger pairs are removed (the whole plan only if it holds nothing else).

This cannot be undone. Choose Cancel to keep everything as it is.

duplicate_plan_names.title: Duplicate Comexio plan names
duplicate_plan_names.description:
Two or more function plans share the exact same name: {plans}.

Comexio doesn't enforce unique plan names — only the internal plan ID actually is unique — but this integration resolves plans by name in several places (Connect, Sort, Restore, …). With duplicate names, a name-based lookup could silently target the wrong plan.

You can technically leave it like this and nothing breaks today, but it's a latent risk — especially for `function_plan_restore`, if that plan is ever deleted and needs restoring. **Recommendation: rename one of the duplicates in Comexio Studio** to remove the ambiguity for good.

knx_dpt_suffix.title: Classify KNX object
knx_dpt_suffix.description:
**{name}** ({remaining} more after this one) uses a KNX DPT1.x subtype (Schalter/Bool/Freigabe/Flanke/Binärwert) that KNX allows to wire as a real toggle switch, a momentary push-button (Taster), or a read-only status readback — the datapoint type alone can't tell which, only you know the actual wiring.

How should this object be treated?

orphaned_backups.title: Backups of a deleted function plan
orphaned_backups.description:
Comexio has no function plan **{plan_name}** under ID {fub_id} any more — it was deleted or renamed. Plan now using ID {fub_id}: **{current_plan}**. If that is this plan under a new name, its newer backups are stored under that name; these are the ones from before.

Its {count} backup(s) are kept for {months} month(s) after the newest one ({newest}) — that period has passed.

**Keep** keeps these backups and never asks again for this plan. You can still delete them later with the **Function Plan Delete Backups** action.
**Delete** removes them for good.

**Load into the plan preview** shows the newest backup in the plan card (the **Plan** selector switches to **Orphaned plans**) without deciding anything — this repair stays open. There you can also browse, restore (as a new plan), delete or keep them. To see what the plan contained first: Developer tools → Actions → **Function Plan Visualize**, field **Snapshot** → pick an entry starting with **{plan_name} — fub {fub_id}**. More in the [backup guide]({docs_url}).

function_plan_vanished.title: Watched function plan not found
function_plan_vanished.description:
The watched function plan **{plan_name}** (ID {fub_id}) was not found in Comexio: ID {fub_id} now holds the plan **{current_name}**. Either the plan was renamed, or it was deleted and Comexio gave its ID to another plan.

**Take over the rename** is offered when the content of {current_name} matches the last backup of {plan_name} but the integration could not follow the rename on its own (normally it does): the watchdog then watches {current_name}, and the backups of {plan_name} continue under the new name. The same content does not prove it is the same plan (e.g. two empty plans).
**Watch {current_name} instead** watches the plan now holding the ID; the backups stay as they are.
**Restore** rebuilds {plan_name} from its newest backup as a new plan and starts it; it stays watched under its new ID.
**Stop watching** removes {plan_name} from the watched user plans.

reference_catalog_mismatch.title: Comexio function block not usable ({server_id})
reference_catalog_mismatch.description:
Comexio {version} on this server does not provide the function block(s) **{blocks}** in the layout this integration was built for. Features that place these blocks in function plans (trigger markers `[TRIG]`) are disabled so no broken elements are written.

**[Report this on GitHub]({issue_url})** — opens a new issue with the diagnosis already filled in (versions and Comexio block catalog only, no personal data). Please review it and submit; a GitHub account is required.

If an entry reads "reference file unusable", the reference files of the aiocomexio library are missing or damaged — please report it.

reference_catalog_unchecked.title: Comexio function block check did not run ({server_id})
reference_catalog_unchecked.description:
The integration could not check which function blocks Comexio {version} on this server provides ({reason}). Until the check succeeds, features that place the block(s) **{blocks}** in function plans (trigger markers `[TRIG]`) are disabled so no broken elements are written.

This is not a sign of an incompatible firmware. The check runs again on every poll and this repair disappears once it succeeds. If it stays, check the Home Assistant log and **[report it on GitHub]({issue_url})**.

unsupported_io_types.title: Comexio IOs without an entity ({server_id})
unsupported_io_types.description:
Comexio reports these IOs as outputs although they carry a meter reading (unit {units}): **{ios}**. As a writable number they would offer a set point for a reading, so this version creates no entity for them.

**[Report this on GitHub]({issue_url})** — opens a new issue with the IO types already filled in (versions, type ids and IO identifiers only, no names or personal data). Please attach the diagnostics file (Settings → Devices & services → Comexio → ⋮ → Download diagnostics) and a debug log (same page: the top ⋮ menu → Enable debug logging, then the entry's ⋮ → Reload, wait until the integration is loaded, then the top ⋮ menu → Disable debug logging — Home Assistant downloads the log; it may contain names and addresses of your installation, please review it). Then review the issue and submit it; a GitHub account is required. A later version will support these IOs.

{category} import switched off
import_disabled.description:
The **{category}** import is switched off, but Comexio still has what the integration created for it: **{commands} Web-IO command(s)**, {plans} managed function plan(s), {trigger_pairs} trigger pair(s) in the shared trigger plan, {devices} Web-IO device(s), {classes} Web-IO class(es) and {bridge_markers} titled KNX bridge marker(s). The sync does not count these as orphans and leaves them alone.

* **Clean up** deletes the {category} function plans (and its pairs in the shared trigger plan), then the {category} Web-IO device and class with all its commands. For KNX, unused bridge markers get their title cleared as well; one used in an own function plan only loses its suffixes and stays a plain marker. The integration reloads afterwards. This cannot be undone.
* **Ignore** keeps everything and does not ask again — until the import is switched on and later off again.
* **Switch the import on again** creates the {category} entities again.

The HA entities of this category were already removed when the import was switched off.

certificate_changed.title: Comexio certificate changed
certificate_changed.description:
Comexio **{server_id}** ({host}) presents another TLS certificate than the one pinned at setup. Until you decide, Home Assistant sends nothing to it.

Pinned (SHA-256):
`{pinned}`

Presented now (SHA-256):
`{actual}`

Compare the new value with the SHA-256 value Comexio's admin page lists under its certificate hashes. If it matches — for example because a new certificate was generated in Comexio — confirm to pin it; the integration reloads. If it does not match, something else answers in Comexio's place: do not confirm, close this dialog and check your network.

`{actual}`

Nothing was changed. Open the repair again to compare that one.
